extracted.intended_audience: actors, improvisers, theatre teachers, and students of improvisation
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and exercises for theatrical improvisation focused on status, spontaneity, narrative skills, and masks/trance to foster spontaneous creativity and practical scene work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter/section: 'Status' (one of four main sections of the book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists related concepts such as 'play high status', 'play low status', 'status transactions', 'master-servant scene'; indicates practical exercises and techniques exploring status relationships in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book presents techniques and exercises developed to foster spontaneity and overcome self-consciousness; arranged for group practice to stimulate spontaneous creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on building story and scene narrative in improvised performance; organized as a set of specific techniques and exercises useful for developing narrative competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masks and Trance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines use of masks, trance states, hypnosis and related phenomena (terms on page include 'Mask class', 'full Mask', 'trance', 'trancers', 'hypnosis', 'transmarginal inhibition') as tools for character work and altered states in performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept / Give (vs Block)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core improvisation principle terms listed on page: 'accept', 'give', 'block'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied evaluative rule: accept and build on offers ('give') rather than blocking them; 'block' is presented as a negative/anti-pattern to avoid in improvisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicality and Character (posture, movement, body, face)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes physical choices (posture, movement, facial work, use of props/space) as key criteria for creating distinct characters and clear stage pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Engagement and Laughter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience response (laughter, engagement) is an implied outcome measure for comedic/improvised work; exercises and techniques are offered to generate ‘funny’ moments and audience reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Types and Examples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of archetypes, role types, and named scene examples (e.g., master-servant) to teach character creation and status dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination and Idea Generation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on generating strong ideas and imaginative choices as criteria for compelling improvisation; book presents exercises to stimulate idea production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching/Exercises and Practical Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Book 'sets out the specific techniques and exercises which Johnstone has himself found most useful and most stimulating.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text functions as a practical manual: criteria for good work include successful application of the exercises and techniques across status/spontaneity/narrative/mask modules; arranged 'more or less in the order a group might approach them.'
